speaker: Bhupinder Singh Hooda
quote_english: There will be no power shortage this summer. The state is self sufficient in power.
summary: Haryana experienced power shortages and outages during the 2013 summer; official data recorded a 9% peak shortage in April-December 2012 and a hydro-related supply crisis hit the state in June 2013.

transcript_sources.title: Economic Times: No power shortage during summers: Haryana CM Bhupinder Singh Hooda

evidence.title: Govt enhanced unallocated power of North to mitigate power shortage of Haryana
evidence.key_figure: Haryana peak power shortage for April to December 2012 was 9%; central unallocated power was raised in June 2012 to mitigate shortage

evidence.title: Himachal rains shut hydropower plants, trigger power crisis in Punjab, Haryana and Delhi
evidence.key_figure: Himachal hydropower plants shut for four days; official sources reported power shortage in northern states including Haryana

analysis:
Hooda's assurance was made on 27 April 2013. A PIB release reproduced by EPR Magazine put Haryana's peak power shortage at 9% for April-December 2012 and said the Centre raised the state's unallocated power in June 2012 to mitigate shortage.

In June 2013, Himachal Pradesh hydro plants shut for four days and India Today reported a power crisis in Punjab, Haryana and Delhi. The Sunday Guardian reported on 9 June 2013 that Haryana's 'power cut-free summer' promise was a mirage and that Gurgaon faced unscheduled outages.

The 9% figure is for the period before Hooda's statement. The June 2013 reporting documents outages during the summer he described as shortage-free.
notes: No single official state-wide shortage percentage for the 2013 summer was located; the verdict rests on the preceding official 9% peak-shortage figure and contemporaneous outage reporting. [ingest: 1 dead evidence link(s) removed]
